metadata.description: Closed-loop optimization to identify NaCl concentration that maximizes anodic peak current at 0.3 V using cyclic voltammetry.

hazards: Salt dust inhalation during solid dispensing
handling_precautions: Wear safety goggles and lab coat
Ensure proper grounding of electrochemical equipment
Verify vial integrity before ultrasound mixing
waste_disposal: Dispose NaCl aqueous solutions according to local aqueous salt waste guidelines
Rinse and neutralize electrode wash water before disposal
cross_contamination_risks: Residual electrolyte on working electrode between runs

llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: Closed-loop optimization selected because the objective is to maximize anodic peak current by adaptively adjusting NaCl concentration.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: NaCl mass in a fixed 10 mL final volume controls electrolyte concentration. The search space of 10–500 mg spans dilute to moderately concentrated regimes while remaining within solubility limits. CV window includes 0.3 V to capture anodic peak. Scan rate and step size selected for adequate resolution.
llm_reasoning.objective_selection_logic: Anodic peak current at 0.3 V directly reflects electrochemical response and is appropriate optimization target for maximizing signal.
llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: 1 solid ≤ 8 allowed; 1 liquid ≤ 4 allowed; final volume 10 mL ≤ 10 mL limit; num_samples 12 ≤ 31 vials; parallel_echem_slots 3 ≤ 3 allowed; optimizer block included only for closed_loop_optimization; screening fields left empty.
assumptions: NaCl fully dissolves within specified mass range in 10 mL water
Peak near 0.3 V lies within selected potential window
Electrode cleaning between runs prevents signal drift
